children: Lithuania’s trade deficit narrowed to €643.8 million in July 2026 from €909.2 million in the same month last year, as exports rose much faster than imports.

Exports increased 13.6% year-on-year to €3,353.6 million, mainly due to higher exports of mineral fuels, mineral oils and products of their distillation (62.2%), cereals (3.0%), and machinery and mechanical appliances and parts (18.3%).

Imports rose 3.5% to €3,997.3 million, amid increased imports of mineral fuels, mineral oils and products of their distillation (17.1%), electrical machinery and equipment and parts (8.8%), and organic chemicals (53.1%).
For the January-July period, Lithuania’s trade deficit widened slightly to €4,198.6 million from €4,148.3 million a year ago.
During this period, Lithuania’s goods were primarily exported to Latvia, which accounted for 13.4% of total exports, followed by Poland (12.2%) and Germany (9.1%).
Imports were sourced predominantly from Poland (13.8%), Germany (12.7%), and Latvia (8.4%).

title: Lithuania Trade Deficit Narrows in July
